identity_marker: bright golden-yellow oblong Ataulfo mango and small paring knife
continuity_anchors: resting on a rustic wooden cutting board under bright, natural kitchen lighting
video_goal: Demonstrate how to cut and invert an Ataulfo mango into a hedgehog shape for easy cubing.
single_prompt: A close-up shot shows hands placing a bright golden-yellow oblong Ataulfo mango and small paring knife side-by-side on a rustic wooden cutting board under bright, natural kitchen lighting. The camera shifts to a first-person view as the left hand holds the mango upright, while the right hand positions the knife slightly off-center at the top stem. The camera moves to a close-up as the knife slices smoothly down the length of the mango, separating one thick, fleshy cheek from the flat central pit. Transitioning to an over-the-shoulder view, the right hand lifts the cut mango cheek off the board, turning the bright orange inner flesh toward the camera. The camera returns to a first-person view as the left hand cradles the mango cheek skin-side down in the palm, bringing the tip of the paring knife to the top edge of the flesh. In an extreme close-up, the knife tip scores three parallel vertical lines down through the flesh, stopping just before piercing the bottom skin. The camera pulls back slightly to a close-up as the left hand rotates the cradled mango cheek 90 degrees. Moving back to an extreme close-up, the knife scores horizontal lines across the previous cuts, creating a distinct crosshatch grid pattern in the bright orange flesh. The camera shifts to a first-person view as the right hand sets down the knife, and both hands grip the outer edges of the scored mango cheek, placing thumbs against the center of the skin underneath. In a close-up, the thumbs push firmly upward, inverting the skin and forcing the crosshatched mango cubes to fan outward into a spiky hedgehog shape. Transitioning to an over-the-shoulder view, the left hand holds the inverted hedgehog mango over a glass bowl, while the right hand uses the paring knife to scrape along the base of the cubes. Finally, in a close-up, the perfectly square Ataulfo mango cubes detach from the skin and tumble down into the glass bowl.
